units.text: INT. PYGMALION - CONTINUOUS
PICKERING [quietly] He ought to, Eliza. [To Doolittle] Why has she changed her mind?
DOOLITTLE [sadly] Intimidated, Governor.
Intimidated.
Middle class morality claims its victim.
Won’t you put on your hat, Liza, and come and see me turned off?
If the Colonel says I must, I—I’ll
units.name: LIZA

units.text: almost sobbing.
I’ll demean myself. And get insulted for my pains, like enough.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: Don’t be afraid: she never comes to words with anyone now, poor woman! respectability has broke all the spirit out of her.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: PICKERING [squeezing Eliza’s elbow gently] Be kind to them, Eliza.
Make the best of it.
LIZA [forcing a little smile for him through her vexation] Oh well, just to show there’s no ill feeling.
I’ll be back in a moment. [She goes out].
DOOLITTLE [sitting down beside Pickering] I feel uncommon nervous about the ceremony, Colonel.
I wish you’d come and see me through it.
But you’ve been through it before, man. You were married to Eliza’s mother.
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: Who told you that, Colonel?
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: Well, nobody told me. But I concluded naturally—
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: No: that ain’t the natural way, Colonel: it’s only the middle class way. My way was always the undeserving way. But don’t say nothing to Eliza. She don’t know: I always had a delicacy about telling her.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: Quite right. We’ll leave it so, if you don’t mind.
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: And you’ll come to the church, Colonel, and put me through straight?
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: With pleasure. As far as a bachelor can.
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: May I come, Mr. Doolittle? I should be very sorry to miss your wedding.
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: I should indeed be honored by your condescension, ma’am; and my poor old woman would take it as a tremenjous compliment. She’s been very low, thinking of the happy days that are no more.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: HIGGINS
units.name: MRS

units.text: rising.
I’ll order the carriage and get ready.
units.name: MRS

units.text: The men rise, except Higgins.
I shan’t be more than fifteen minutes.
units.name: MRS

units.text: As she goes to the door Eliza comes in, hatted and buttoning her gloves.
I’m going to the church to see your father married, Eliza. You had better come in the brougham with me. Colonel Pickering can go on with the bridegroom.
units.name: MRS

units.text: Mrs. Higgins goes out.
Eliza comes to the middle of the room between the centre window and the ottoman.
Pickering joins her.
Bridegroom! What a word! It makes a man realize his position, somehow.
units.name: DOOLITTLE

units.text: He takes up his hat and goes towards the door.
Before I go, Eliza, do forgive him and come back to us.
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: I don’t think papa would allow me. Would you, dad?
units.name: LIZA

units.text: DOOLITTLE [sad but magnanimous] They played you off very cunning, Eliza, them two sportsmen.
If it had been only one of them, you could have nailed him.
But you see, there was two; and one of them chaperoned the other, as you might say. [To Pickering] It was artful of you, Colonel; but I bear no malice: I should have done the same myself.
I been the victim of one woman after another all my life; and I don’t grudge you two getting the better of Eliza.
I shan’t interfere.
It’s time for us to go, Colonel.
So long, Henry.
See you in St. George’s, Eliza. [He goes out].
PICKERING [coaxing] Do stay with us, Eliza. [He follows Doolittle].
Eliza goes out on the balcony to avoid being alone with Higgins.
He rises and joins her there.
She immediately comes back into the room and makes for the door; but he goes along the balcony quickly and gets his back to the door before she reaches it.
Well, Eliza, you’ve had a bit of your own back, as you call it. Have you had enough? and are you going to be reasonable? Or do you want any more?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: You want me back only to pick up your slippers and put up with your tempers and fetch and carry for you.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: I haven’t said I wanted you back at all.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Oh, indeed. Then what are we talking about?
units.name: LIZA

units.text: About you, not about me. If you come back I shall treat you just as I have always treated you. I can’t change my nature; and I don’t intend to change my manners. My manners are exactly the same as Colonel Pickering’s.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: That’s not true. He treats a flower girl as if she was a duchess.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: And I treat a duchess as if she was a flower girl.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: I see.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: She turns away composedly, and sits on the ottoman, facing the window.
The same to everybody.
units.name: LIZA

units.text: Just so.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Like father.
units.name: LIZA
